title: confiture migrate diff --format json
description: Report from `migrate diff`: the structural changes between the current state (a schema file, a directory of DDL files, stdin, or the configured database) and the desired state (a schema file, a directory such as `fraiseql compile --emit-ddl` writes, or stdin), and the migration file written when `--generate` was given.

success.description: False when either side could not be read or parsed; `error` says why.

irreversible_reason.description: `data` when the change drops a table or a column: the generated down file recreates the object, never its rows. Null otherwise.

details.description: The change as one line (`ADD TABLE tb_post`), naming the table the way the schema file names it — `ADD COLUMN tenant.tb_meter.x` for a qualified declaration, `ADD TABLE tb_post` for an unqualified one. Confiture never invents a `public.` qualifier the file did not write.

migration_file.description: The generated file's name under --migrations-dir, or null: the .up.sql of the pair when the desired state came through --from/--to, the .py file for positional schema files.

destructive_gate.description: The destructive-gate policy the generated migration was written under (migration.destructive, overridden by --allow-destructive / --forbid-destructive): `gated` marks a data-losing file with `-- confiture:destructive` so `migrate up` needs `--allow-destructive`, `allow` leaves it unmarked, `forbid` would have refused. Null when nothing was generated.

source.description: Where the desired state came from; null when the run failed before it was resolved.

kind.description: `sql`: DDL text. Reserved for a structured export (`json`) when one exists.

path.description: The file or directory, or `-` for stdin.

warnings.description: What the comparison has to say that is not a change: an object defined more than once in one schema tree, which is not a difference between the two sides but is a reason the diff may be reading a tree `confiture build` does not produce (#313). Warned, never failed — a duplicate definition is `confiture lint`'s problem (`build_001`) and `build --fail-on-duplicates`' problem, both of which already exist and are opt-in. Present and empty when there is nothing to report, never absent-on-success. Defined inline rather than in _common.schema.json because this schema's $id is on a different host, which a relative $ref out of it cannot resolve — as build.schema.json does.

code.description: The error-code registry entry that names the situation (`DIFFER_402` for a duplicate definition), so a consumer matches a code rather than a sentence.

severity.description: The severity the registry publishes for `code`; never `error` here — an error is not a warning, it is the envelope's `error` field.

message.description: What happened, in one line: the object, how many definitions it has, which one the build keeps and which one the comparison used.

file.description: The file it is about, relative to the project root; null when the diff read its sides as concatenated text rather than per file, which is every `migrate diff` today.
